The [SASRec PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py) maps sequences [B,L] through `log2feats` to [B,L,H], then selects `features[:, -1, :]` for inference. Histories must be right-aligned with zero left padding so the final position contains the latest interaction. Candidate embeddings [B,C,H] multiply final features [B,H,1], producing scores [B,C]; shared candidates [C,H] also broadcast correctly. Adapter recommendation: explicitly distinguish shared [C] from per-user [B,C] candidate IDs and preserve the batch axis, including B=1. The reference accepts NumPy inputs; tensor-native adapters should preserve device and integer dtype.

The [reference validation routine](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/utils.py) samples users through Python’s RNG and negatives through NumPy’s RNG. Its 100 negative draws can contain duplicates or the target itself, so it does not match the specified RecHarness protocol. Preserve the pinned evaluator’s 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, exclusions, and seed=42. For independent diagnostics, use isolated RNGs and fixed user/candidate lists across checkpoints; per-user seeds derived deterministically from category and user ID prevent iteration-order dependence. These are integration recommendations, not verified RecHarness internals.

Ranking ties require explicit attention: [PyTorch topk](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html) does not guarantee stable tied indices. [Stable sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.sort.html) preserves input order, enabling deterministic diagnostic rankings with a predefined candidate order. Keep host ranking semantics unchanged; never assume its tie policy matches diagnostic top-k. Compute each user’s hit once, average within category, then average the four category HR@10 values equally.
